questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: The table shows the output of chairs at a factory when different numbers of workers are employed. number of workers 1 2 3 4 5 number of chairs produced 6 17 27 32 30 Diminishing marginal returns to labour will set in when

options.A: the second worker is employed.

options.A: 3 B 4 C 5 D 6

questions.questionText: In 2004 union officials and businessmen in Argentina agreed to increase the minimum wage from 350 to 450 pesos. In which circumstances would such a rise increase employment?

options.A: Investment increases at a more rapid rate than consumption.
options.B: Labour and product markets are competitive.
options.C: The higher wage rate produces a proportionately greater rise in labour productivity.
options.D: The minimum wage is set above the equilibrium level.

questions.questionText: The table gives information about a firm’s costs over a given range of output in the short run and in the long run. output (thousand) 21 22 23 24 25 short-run average cost ($) 20 19 18 17 16 long-run average cost ($) 12 13 14 15 16 Which conclusions can be drawn about the characteristics of production over this output range in the short run and in the long run? short run long run

options.A: decreasing returns to scale diminishing returns
options.C: increasing returns decreasing returns to scale

options.A: v B v + x C v – x D z – x

What could explain why the proportion of total employment in an economy accounted for by small firms decreases?

options.A: a trend towards the use of sub-contractors to produce specialised components
options.B: growing technical economies of scale in manufacturing
options.C: growth of the service sector and a decline in manufacturing
options.D: the opening up of specialist markets as real incomes rise

options.A: B total total revenue revenue TR TR O O output output
options.C: D TR total total revenue revenue TR O O output output

A country’s government reduces the specific tax on packets of cigarettes. What could explain why this leads to an increase in tax revenue from cigarette sales?

options.A: Consumers switch to dearer brands.
options.B: The demand for cigarettes is price-inelastic.
options.C: The price of cigarettes falls by less than the reduction in tax.
options.D: There is a reduction in illegal imports of cigarettes.

questions.questionText: Which is not a policy designed to correct market failure?

options.A: competition policy

Over a given period, money income in an economy increased by 6%. Over the same period, prices rose on average by 4%. What can be deduced from this?

options.A: Real income increased by 2%.
options.B: The income velocity of circulation decreased by 2%.
options.D: The volume of output decreased by 2%.

questions.questionText: A closed economy has a banking system consisting of a single bank. The bank operates with a cash ratio of 10%. Customers deposit $20000 in cash. Assuming subsequent net withdrawals of cash from the banking system are zero, what is the maximum amount of loans that the bank can create?
What will cause the level of investment to fall according to the accelerator model?

options.A: a decrease in business confidence
options.B: a decrease in the rate of growth of national income
options.C: an increase in the price of capital equipment
options.D: an increase in the rate of interest

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government, consumption is 4/5 of income at all levels of income. The present equilibrium level of income is $220 million. The full employment level of income is $240 million. By how much would investment have to increase to reach full employment?

options.A: $2 million B $4 million C $16 million D $20 million

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what will result in a decrease in aggregate demand?

options.A: a decrease in interest rates
options.B: a decrease in the balance of trade deficit
options.C: a decrease in the government’s budget deficit
options.D: a decrease in the household saving ratio

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for loanable funds. The market is in equilibrium at point X. What could be the new equilibrium point if there was a decline in business confidence and an increase in bank lending? S
The diagram shows the contribution of four components of aggregate demand to the change in US real GDP in the four quarters of 2010. key personal consumption
An economic recession leads to an increase in unemployment. Why might this cause a fall in an economy’s long-term growth rate?

options.A: It is impossible to regain consumption lost in recession.
options.B: Rising unemployment is likely to raise real wage levels.
options.C: Social attitudes become less accepting of unemployment.
options.D: There will be a harmful effect on human capital.

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual income thresholds per person used by the World Bank to classify countries according to their nominal Gross National Income (GNI) in 2000 and 2010. 2000 2010 low income $755 or less $1005 or less lower middle $756 to $2995 $1006 to $3975 upper middle $2996 to $9625 $3976 to $12275 high income $9266 or more $12276 or more What could explain the changes recorded in the table?

options.A: Income inequality between countries increased between 2000 and 2010.
options.B: On average, real GNI in low income countries increased by roughly one third between 2000 and 2010.
options.C: On average, world prices increased by roughly one third between 2000 and 2010.
options.D: Some of the countries in the upper middle income category in 2000 were re-classified as high income countries in 2010.

questions.questionText: What is likely to result in an increase in GDP per worker in a developing economy?

options.A: an increase in the employment rate
options.B: an increase in the population of working age
options.C: a shift from working in subsistence agriculture to working in manufacturing
options.D: a shift from working in manufacturing to working in subsistence agriculture

questions.questionText: It is often argued that the present rate of economic growth will soon lead to the exhaustion of reserves of material resources, such as minerals and oil. What does this argument fail to take into account?

options.A: the drawbacks of present GDP levels as an indicator of the ‘happiness’ of the population
options.B: the effect of increasing resource prices on the discovery and exploitation of new reserves
options.C: the right of future generations to enjoy present standards of living
options.D: the role of education in economic development

questions.questionText: What will be the impact of an increase in marginal tax rates?

options.A: an increase in the propensity to save
options.B: an increase in the value of the investment multiplier
options.D: a strengthening in the operation of automatic stabilisers

questions.questionText: A central bank increases interest rates in order to control inflation. What is likely to increase as a result of this?

options.A: firms’ sales revenue

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from a devaluation of the £ sterling?

options.A: an increase in foreign direct investment in the UK by global manufacturing firms
options.B: an increase in the number of UK residents taking holidays abroad
options.C: an increase in the number of UK students applying for places in North American universities
options.D: an increase in the supply of foreign workers seeking temporary employment over the summer in the UK

questions.questionText: A fair trade scheme encourages consumers in developed countries to buy food produced by farming cooperatives in developing countries at a higher price than that charged by commercial firms. Why might this be harmful to economic development?

options.A: It will cause a worsening in the terms of trade of developing economies.
options.B: It will reduce the amount of government aid provided to developing economies.
options.C: It will reduce the prices subsistence farmers receive for their produce.
options.D: It will slow the process of economic diversification in developing economies.
